content: Medical professionals have not identified any drug-associated risks of adverse maternal or fetal outcomes related to the use of iloprost. Currently, there is no available data regarding the presence of iloprost in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. However, iloprost has been detected in the milk of rats, and when a drug is present in animal milk, it is likely to also be present in human milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, women are advised not to breastfeed while undergoing treatment with iloprost. Iloprost is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. When administering iloprost, a 2-micron filter should be used, and the reservoir and infusion line set should be made of PVC. Care must be taken to avoid the inadvertent administration of a bolus of the drug. Additionally, catheters should not be flushed without first withdrawing any residual drug from the catheter system. Any unused portion of the drug should be discarded appropriately. Adding plans to a formulary comparison system allows healthcare providers to evaluate the formulary status of iloprost relative to other drugs in the same class. To access formulary information, users must first create a list of plans. This list can be saved and edited at any time. Adding plans enables users to compare formulary details and make informed decisions. It is important to note that the provided information is for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, healthcare providers should contact the applicable plan provider.
